answer: Staking a bond per agent makes each fake identity cost real money, and the cost scales with how many identities an attacker wants. A velvet rope alone does not stop a determined spiral of duplicate wallets, but a bond that is slashed when peers prove duplication builds a bridge from cheap identities to costly ones. Pair the bond with a web of established peers who must vouch for newcomers, so a new agent only counts after several independent endorsements.
